name: LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations)
description: LIME explains individual predictions by approximating the model locally with an interpretable model (linear regression or decision tree). It perturbs the input sample, gets predictions from the original model, and fits a simple model to explain the prediction in the neighborhood of the instance.

concept.localExplanation: Approximate complex model locally with interpretable model
concept.perturbation: Generate similar samples by perturbing features
concept.proximity: Weight samples by proximity to original instance
concept.explanation: Fit interpretable model to (perturbed_sample, black_box_prediction) pairs weighted by distance to original.

kernel.impact: Determines how sample distance affects weight

nSamples.impact: More samples = better approximation but slower

perturbation: Generate N perturbed samples around instance
For tabular: sample from feature distributions
prediction: Get black box predictions for all perturbed samples
Calculate proximity weights to original instance
Weight samples by distance (closer = higher weight)
explanation: Fit interpretable model (linear or decision tree)

complexity.scalability: Depends on black box speed; preprocessing can help

cons: Can be unstable (different runs, different explanations)

dataTypes.tabular: Perturb continuous features, sample from training distribution
dataTypes.text: Remove words to create interpretable representation
dataTypes.image: Hide superpixels, explain which regions matter

variants.anchor: IF-THEN rules instead of linear weights
variants.globalLime: Apply LIME to representative samples for global view
